# Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience

**Company:** Verdane Care (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Graz, Austria (hybrid) or fully remote within Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent (or B2B contract in Croatia on request)
**Team:** Patient Experience squad (4 engineers, 1 designer, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Verdane Care makes appointment-booking and follow-up software for private clinics and physiotherapy practices. Patients use our web app and mobile web experience to book visits, fill in intake forms, receive reminders and view exercise plans.

As a Full-Stack Engineer you will build and improve those patient-facing features end to end – from React components and accessibility to the Node.js APIs and the database behind them. You will work in a small squad with a designer and a product manager, and you will ship to production several times a week.

## What you will do

- Build new patient-facing features in React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and performance on low-end phones
- Implement Node.js (NestJS) APIs and PostgreSQL schemas to support those features
- Integrate with third-party systems such as clinic calendars, SMS providers and payment gateways
- Write unit, integration and end-to-end tests (Jest, Playwright) and keep the build green
- Take part in design reviews, usability sessions and sprint planning
- Handle personal health data responsibly: follow our GDPR and data-minimisation guidelines, support audit requests from clinic customers
- Mentor interns or junior colleagues when the opportunity arises

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
- Experience writing backend services in Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and working with SQL databases
- Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
- Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
- Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10) and willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
- Fluent English; German or Croatian is helpful for customer-facing conversations

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Next.js or other server-side rendering frameworks
- Experience in healthcare, wellness or other regulated environments
- Familiarity with AWS or a similar cloud, and with Docker
- Experience with design systems and Storybook
- Experience with analytics and A/B testing

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 54,000 – 70,000 gross per year depending on experience (Austrian collective agreement minimum applies)
- 25 days of holiday plus the Austrian public holidays, 5 additional well-being days and a EUR 1,200 yearly education budget
- Flexible hours, a home-office stipend and a yearly team retreat
- A friendly, low-ego team that cares about the people who use our software

Send your CV. A short cover letter and a link to something you have built (a portfolio, a GitHub project or a live site) are welcome but optional. We reply within ten working days.

Verdane Care is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from career changers and people returning to work.

It highlights particularly persuasive evidence: BankID authentication, a 61% to 74% onboarding-conversion improvement, secure document handling, WCAG 2.1 AA, mobile LCP improvement from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds, React Native delivery, and production technologies. The tone is confident without making unsupported seniority or healthcare claims. The main content weakness is that the letter is slightly longer and more repetitive than necessary for a cover letter described as short. The third paragraph repeats React, HTML/CSS, mobile performance, and accessibility points, while several technologies are listed without directly explaining their relevance to the role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly parseable: it uses standard prose, no tables or unusual formatting, and includes strong matching keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, authentication, accessibility, WCAG, Jest, Playwright, GitHub Actions, Docker, AWS, Next.js, Figma, and React Native. It should perform well in keyword-based and AI screening, with an estimated high AI screening probability because the evidence is specific and closely aligned with the role. It could improve further by using the job's exact concepts of semantic HTML, responsive layouts, unit testing, end-to-end testing, and regulated environments where the candidate's material supports them. The letter does not mention OWASP Top 10, and the candidate information does not establish that the candidate has that knowledge, so it should not be added merely for keyword matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is very strong for the core engineering requirements. The letter demonstrates substantially more than the required React/TypeScript experience and directly connects Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, Docker, testing, accessibility, performance, authentication, document security, and A/B testing to real outcomes. The fintech/KYC background is a credible adjacent regulated-environment experience, although it is not healthcare experience. The principles paragraph aligns well with Patients first, Privacy by default, and Simple beats clever. The letter does not establish willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements, and the candidate information does not explicitly provide that statement; this remains an unaddressed requirement rather than a rewriting opportunity. OWASP Top 10 awareness is also not evidenced in the supplied candidate information. German is only school-level and therefore is not a strength for customer-facing conversations. The letter also does not mention mentoring, although the original information supports the coding-bootcamp mentor experience and this could be included if space permits.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR — In the third paragraph beginning “I’d bring practical experience improving accessibility and performance,” remove the repetitive sentences “I build web interfaces with HTML and CSS and have improved mobile performance and accessibility in customer-facing flows.” The same evidence is already established by the WCAG and LCP results. Replace that sentence with a concise, more role-specific statement such as: “I build accessible, responsive interfaces with React, HTML, and CSS, and I use Jest and Playwright for unit and end-to-end testing.” Only use “responsive” if the candidate is comfortable standing behind that description; the original material supports mobile performance work and HTML/CSS but does not explicitly document responsive-layout implementation.

MINOR — In the same third paragraph, replace the technology-list sentence “I work with automated unit and end-to-end testing using Jest and Playwright, and with Git-based delivery through GitHub Actions, Docker, and AWS” with a more precise version: “I use Jest and Playwright for automated testing and GitHub Actions for Git-based delivery, with Docker and AWS in the delivery environment.” This makes the relationship between the tools clearer and avoids implying that Docker and AWS are themselves Git-based workflows.

MINOR — In the paragraph beginning “Although my background is in fintech,” change “my background is in fintech rather than healthcare” to “my background is in fintech, a regulated environment, rather than healthcare.” This truthfully makes the adjacent regulated-environment experience more visible for the nice-to-have requirement without claiming healthcare experience.

MINOR — To keep the letter short and focused, either remove the React Native sentence from the third paragraph or shorten the technology list in that paragraph. If retaining it, use: “Earlier, I led most of a React Native ferry-ticket app that reached approximately 50,000 downloads.” This preserves a strong delivery and mobile-product result while reducing wording.
